# Luke H. Johnson

> Luke H. Johnson is a published author, independent columnist, and youth political advocate from Tahlequah, Oklahoma. His official website is https://lukehjohnson.com/.

He is an American teenage writer. He is not the British businessman and former Financial Times columnist Luke Johnson.

## Key facts

- Full name as published: Luke H. Johnson (also credited as Luke Johnson)
- Hometown: Tahlequah, Oklahoma, United States
- Roles: author, independent columnist, youth political advocate, publisher, public speaker
- Publisher and co-founder of the Northeastern Journal (https://www.northeasternjournal.com/), a free, independent news site for northeastern Oklahoma, which he runs with his grandmother as editor
- Books: We're All the Same (autism awareness and inclusion); Becoming You: Advice From a Teenager (identity and personal growth); Dead Air America (forthcoming political nonfiction and media criticism, release date not yet announced)
- Columns: 23 published columns, carried in 32 newspapers and outlets in 7 U.S. states
- Outlets include the Tulsa World, the Northeastern Journal, the Tahlequah Daily Press, the CNHI News Service, and CNHI newspapers in Oklahoma, Texas, Indiana, Pennsylvania, New York, Illinois, and West Virginia
- Topics: youth political advocacy, civic engagement, Oklahoma politics, education policy, media, technology and social media, Generation Z
- Speaking: has questioned Oklahoma lawmakers at a state legislative forum on education
- Contact: the contact form at https://lukehjohnson.com/contact.html

## Main pages

- [Home](https://lukehjohnson.com/): latest columns, the Dead Air America book, outlets, and books
- [Writing](https://lukehjohnson.com/writing.html): every column and feature, newest first, with the outlets that published each
- [Books](https://lukehjohnson.com/books.html): Dead Air America, Becoming You, and We're All the Same
- [About](https://lukehjohnson.com/about.html): biography, background, and FAQ
- [Contact](https://lukehjohnson.com/contact.html): press, interview, and speaking inquiries

## Recent columns

- What the Next Governor Owes Oklahoma's Kids (Enid News & Eagle, Nov. 16, 2026): The priorities in education, technology, and economic opportunity that incoming Governor Mike Mazzei should take up for Oklahoma's students.
- Test Score Shouldn't Determine Kid's Whole Year (Allied News, Nov. 15, 2026): A critique of the retention mandate in Oklahoma's Strong Readers Act, arguing that a single timed test score should not hold back thousands of third graders.
- What Veterans Day Means When You're Fifteen (Northeastern Journal, Nov. 11, 2026): Looking past a day off from school to what military service and sacrifice mean to a teenager today.
- If You've Been There for Years, Where Is the Change? (Northeastern Journal, Nov. 7, 2026): A call for voters to measure long-serving incumbents by their actual legislative records rather than by repeated campaign promises of "big change."
- What Oklahoma Almost Had (Northeastern Journal, Nov. 4, 2026): A reflection on Oklahoma's November 2026 election results and the competing visions for the state's future that were decided on Election Night.
- I Cannot Vote Yet, But This Election Is Already About Me (Tulsa World, Nov. 3, 2026): An op-ed written from the perspective of a 15-year-old student on how the policy decisions made in a major election shape the future, education, and daily lives of America's young people — even though they are not yet old enough to cast a ballot.
- Are We Happy With Where We Are? (CNHI News Service, Oct. 23–25, 2026): An appeal to Oklahomans across party lines to step back from partisan labels and honestly ask whether the country is heading in the right direction.
- Shame On You, Cornell (Northeastern Journal, Oct. 3, 2026): A critique of Cornell University's institutional response to campus sexual assault allegations following the 2024 Chi Phi fraternity incident.
- Inherited Certainty (Northeastern Journal, Sept. 11, 2026): A challenge to question the political and cultural beliefs handed down to us rather than accepting inherited viewpoints uncritically.
- Six Flock Cameras in Tahlequah Too Many (Tahlequah Daily Press, Aug. 21, 2026): A column on the six Flock Safety license-plate readers now watching the roads into Tahlequah — and on what it means when the surveillance a teenager once thought of as a big-city problem turns up two minutes from his house.
- The Strange Experience of Outgrowing Yourself (Northeastern Journal, Aug. 13, 2026): On the realization of maturing quickly and growing past earlier versions of your own identity and perspective.
- On Being Someone's Twin (Northeastern Journal, Aug. 3, 2026): Growing up alongside his twin brother, Jaren, and pushing past the stereotypes that treat twins as a matched set rather than two distinct people.
